requirements.quote:
Since the owner name is not known, any domain name
can be used as a placeholder (and is ignored).
requirements.condition: When constructing an inverse query whose owner name is unknown.
requirements.required_behavior: Any domain name may be used as the owner-name placeholder.
requirements.why_checkable: The query constructor can be checked for its permitted placeholder owner names; this is permission and does not require choosing a particular name.

requirements.quote:
Since the owner name is not known, any domain name
can be used as a placeholder (and is ignored).
requirements.condition: When processing the owner-name placeholder in an inverse query.
requirements.why_checkable: The inverse-query matching path can be inspected or exercised with different placeholder names to verify that the name does not affect matching.

requirements.quote:
A single octet of zero,
signifying the root, is usually used because it minimizes the length of
the message.
requirements.condition: When constructing the owner-name placeholder in an inverse query.
requirements.required_behavior: A single zero octet may be used as the root owner-name placeholder; this choice is customary rather than mandatory.
requirements.why_checkable: The inverse-query encoding can be checked for the permitted single-zero-octet root placeholder, without requiring every query to choose it.

requirements.quote:
This query asks for a question whose answer is the Internet style
address 10.1.0.52.  Since the owner name is not known, any domain name
can be used as a placeholder (and is ignored).  A single octet of zero,
signifying the root, is usually used because it minimizes the length of
the message.  The TTL of the RR is not significant.
requirements.condition: When processing the resource record in an inverse query.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the query resource record TTL as insignificant for the inverse lookup.
requirements.why_checkable: The matching path can be inspected or exercised with varying query TTL values to verify that the TTL does not constrain the inverse lookup.

requirements.quote:
Note that the QTYPE in a response to an inverse query is the same as the
TYPE field in the answer section of the inverse query.
requirements.condition: When constructing a question in a response to an inverse query.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the response question QTYPE equal to the TYPE field in the inverse query answer section.
requirements.why_checkable: The response question QTYPE can be directly compared with the corresponding inverse query answer TYPE.

requirements.quote:
Responses to
inverse queries may contain multiple questions when the inverse is not
unique.
requirements.condition: When the inverse lookup is not unique.
requirements.required_behavior: The inverse-query response may contain multiple questions.
requirements.why_checkable: Response construction can be checked for the permitted multiple-question form when there are multiple inverse matches; multiple questions are allowed, not required.

requirements.quote:
If the question section in the response is not empty, then the
RR in the answer section is modified to correspond to be an exact copy
of an RR at the first QNAME.
requirements.condition: When an inverse-query response has a nonempty question section.
requirements.required_behavior: Modify the resource record in the response answer section to be an exact copy of a resource record at the first response QNAME.
requirements.why_checkable: The response answer resource record can be compared field by field with a stored resource record at the first response question name.
